summary.headline: MCX Q1 FY27 total income rose 85% YoY to INR752 crores and PAT reached INR413 crores, though revenue fell sequentially from an exceptional Q4 FY26.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR752 crores (+85% YoY), revenue from operations of INR702 crores (+88% YoY), EBITDA of INR544 crores (about 72% margin) and PAT of INR413 crores. Management described Q1 as a consolidation after an exceptionally strong Q4 FY26, with ADT at INR10.5 lakh crores and futures ADT up 47% YoY. Bullion options premium ratio fell sharply as volatility normalised, while notional volumes rose, and management said bullion volumes were softer in the quarter. Management said the RBI bank guarantee rule (in force from July) is not expected to be significantly detrimental, and that it is more a Q2 issue.

financial_highlights.metric: Bullion options premium ADT vs notional
financial_highlights.change: premium ADT down 27% QoQ, notional up about 116% QoQ

segments.name: Energy (crude, natural gas, electricity)
segments.commentary: Crude and natural gas form a large share of volume; crude options volume was flat QoQ despite three months of heightened prices. Electricity futures Q1 ADT about INR37 crores with about 55% ADT market share and about 1,630 lots open interest.

segments.name: Bullion (gold, silver)
segments.commentary: Gold options ADV about 300 metric tons (+100% QoQ) and silver about 9,400 metric tons (about +2% QoQ) per management. Silver all-variant options open interest rose to 583 tonnes from 522 tonnes; gold to 17.3 tonnes from 16.9. Management said bullion numbers were softer in the quarter.

segments.name: Indices and metals
segments.commentary: BULLDEX index product is being reworked in futures and options; management expects it to lift indices. Metals options headroom cited, particularly copper after warehouse and contract rationalisation, with no launch dates given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth momentum at the fundamental level to continue; Q4 FY26 exceptional numbers will weigh on YoY comparisons.
Management expects FY27 to be strong, but said macro-driven spikes are outside its control.
Bank guarantee regulation: not expected to be significantly detrimental; cost-of-funds impact on some member flows expected to be optimal as industry adapts.
Data services plans and more clarity on revenue from AMC use of MCX bullion price to be shared over the next couple of quarters.
Several indices products expected to hit the market over the next few months.
capex_capacity: Technology capacity: handled more than 3 billion transactions a day versus under 1 billion a year earlier, with capacity to handle more than double that.
MCX Coal Exchange of India incorporated; at a very early stage with procedural steps underway; not a derivatives initiative yet.
Silver 100 gram futures launched in the quarter in response to silver prices and received well.
Good Delivery norms expanded to include silver, with the country's first domestic silver refiner and three more domestic gold refiners empanelled.
demand_pricing: Bullion options: management attributed the premium ratio decline mainly to lower volatility in gold and silver; it said contract mix and participation shifts were not significant drivers.
Competition: challenger exchanges are active in adjacent equity segments; management said main head-on contracts have held, with some competitor expiry-date changes under review.

New members: 12 added in the quarter. FPIs: 35 added, taking the count to about 220, with FPIs about 2.5% of the INR10 lakh-plus crore base. FPI expansion to non-energy contracts awaits SEBI progress.
UCCs: flat QoQ after strong prior quarters; management said no target number was given, but FY26 closed at 20 lakh UCCs.
Uncertainty: management could not quantify the share of trades backed by bank guarantees.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI bank guarantee rule on volumes, and why are gold and silver premiums falling while notional rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rule is more a Q2 issue, with no significant detrimental impact seen yet. The premium fall reflects normalising volatility; ADT grew from about INR3 lakh crores a year earlier to INR6.6 lakh crores in Q4 and INR10.5 lakh crores in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the sequential decline in SGF contribution (investor protection fund) differ from the revenue decline, and what drove the employee cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Chandresh Shah said SGF contribution follows SEBI's monthly methodology plus management's buffer choice. Employee cost rose from hiring, increments and higher variable pay in a subsidiary; a one-time 8-9% element will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the bullion premium decline is due to volatility, contract mix, or participation?
qa_highlights.answer: Praveen DG said volatility normalisation was the main driver; premiums for gold and silver are at similar levels and participation was stable, so contract mix and OTM shifts were not significant.

qa_highlights.question: Is technology capacity adequate for volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has handled more than 3 billion transactions a day, up from under 1 billion a year earlier, with capacity to handle more than double that. Sanjay Rajpal, the new Executive Director for Critical Operations, is focused on resilience and cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the electricity futures market share and open interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Electricity futures Q1 ADT was about INR37 crores with about 55% ADT market share and about 1,630 lots open interest (over 70% market share in open interest).

qa_highlights.question: What is the float income and what is the revenue opportunity from AMC use of MCX bullion prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Float income was about INR30 crores. Management said the AMC benchmark use is at an early stage with no separate revenue quantified; data services plans will be shared over the next couple of quarters.

risks_watch: RBI bank guarantee rule (effective in July after a 90-day absorption window) could raise member cost of funds and affect prop-trading volumes; the impact is unquantified.
Sequential revenue decline from exceptional Q4 FY26; YoY comparisons will be tough in coming quarters.
Bullion premium ratio compression (1.03% to 0.35%) hurts transaction revenue per notional unit if volatility stays low.
Competition from challenger exchanges in commodity segments, including expiry-date changes.
Pending SEBI decisions on FPI participation in non-energy contracts, the commodity derivatives department, and open items on SBI position limits and co-location.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural growth and product pipeline, but cautious and non-committal on near-term volumes, bank guarantee impact and FPI timelines. Management repeatedly framed Q1 as a normalisation after Q4 and declined to quantify several questions (bank guarantee share, UCC targets, regulatory timelines).
key_quotes: So, what we are seeing this quarter, it's a normalization of that without some of those sort of very strong geopolitical factors playing in at that same extent, but with some of the fundamental and foundational growth elements still continuing to be strong.
We are not expecting this to have a very significant detrimental impact.
So, capacity-wise, very well positioned as we speak in terms of the growth that is coming our way, but we continue to look to drive resiliency, looking at driving scale.

adds.what: Technology capacity to handle more than 3 billion transactions a day (vs under 1 billion a year earlier), with headroom to more than double

growth.why: Management expects FY27 to be on strong momentum but gave no numbers; backing is aspirational (new indices products, BULLDEX rework, metals options headroom, FPI expansion awaiting SEBI) with no launch dates or quantified orders, and Q4 FY26 exceptional base will weigh on YoY comparisons.
